title: Design a Prompt Experiment Workbench

response.placeholder: Define an immutable run manifest before designing queues or dashboards.
response.reference_answer:
## Contract and durable state

A prompt draft is editable, but publishing creates an immutable `PromptVersion` with its template, variable schema, policy revision, and owner. A `Run` stores the exact prompt version, approved model/config version, dataset snapshot, evaluator version, caller identity, and idempotency key. The run manifest is written before returning acceptance; a comparison names two completed run IDs rather than recomputing against moving defaults.

## Execution path

The API validates template variables and authorization, estimates a bounded budget, records a queued run, and writes an outbox event. Tenant-aware schedulers enforce both concurrent-run and token/cost limits. Workers lease one run with a fencing token, resolve immutable inputs, and write append-only per-case results. Progress is an advisory stream derived from durable counters; reconnecting clients read the durable run state. Cancellation is a durable transition checked before dispatching the next case and before publishing aggregate results.

## Reproducibility and comparison

A run records model provider revision where available, decoding parameters, seed policy, input snapshot hash, and evaluator implementation version. The comparison service aligns cases by snapshot identity and reports missing, skipped, safety-filtered, and failed cases separately. It must not label a run better merely because one side silently omitted expensive or failed examples.

## Security and lifecycle

Keep templates, inputs, outputs, and logs in tenant-scoped storage; authorize each artifact read independently. Redact or encrypt sensitive payloads, keep only bounded diagnostic excerpts, and audit publication, sharing, export, and deletion. A share link carries a scoped principal and expiry, never a raw storage URL. Retention jobs delete artifacts while preserving minimal aggregate/accounting records where policy permits.

## Evaluation and operations

Track evaluator score distributions, pairwise win rate with confidence intervals, cost per completed case, and safety/format failure rates by prompt and model version. Separately monitor queue age, lease expiry, retry rate, provider errors, cancellation latency, budget rejects, and redaction failures. These metrics prevent a provider outage or a changed test set from masquerading as prompt quality.

## Progressive Hints

1. A draft is not enough information to reproduce a run.
2. Progress delivery is not the persistence boundary.
3. Compare like-for-like case snapshots, including failures.
4. A shared result link needs its own access and expiry policy.
